result.summary: ELIXIR-DEV rebased this branch onto origin/main (which had moved to include ISS-0190/0191/0192/0194 concurrently), verified zero conflict markers, and committed a claim -- then stopped, its own final message stating it was 'waiting for a background test monitor' to notify it, a runtime capability a spawned subagent does not have. It never returned. ORCH completed the remaining mechanical steps directly, per the same authority already exercised for this run's own Step 00 (git-setup, logged ORCH -> - at run start) -- git-merge procedure is not source/test/doc content. Before acting, ORCH verified the rebase's actual state rather than trusting the stalled agent's own claim: zero conflict markers (git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U), a clean mix compile --warnings-as-errors, and a clean 20/20 re-run of this branch's own test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs. That last check surfaced a real side effect of the dead run: 6 orphaned erl.exe 'mix test' processes (the ISS-0107 Windows fake-mix recursion bug TEST-RUNNER had already diagnosed and cleaned once on this same run) had re-accumulated and saturated the shared Postgres pool (pg_stat_activity unreachable, then 38 connections once psql itself connected). Killed all 6 (Stop-Process -Force) and confirmed the pool recovered (letflow/letflow_dev reachable, test passing 20/20) before proceeding. Pushed the rebased branch with --force-with-lease -- scoped to this run's own feature branch only, per GIT_MERGE.md step 6 (ISS-0210, merged earlier today); this is that rule's first live exercise on an actual code branch. Opened PR #420 with the real mix test counts (1292 passed, 2 failed, 0 attributable, routes 1+3 named) in the body per core-directives.md's Never-Call-a-Red-Pipeline-OK rule. gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch: the GitHub-side merge succeeded (confirmed via gh pr view --json state,mergedAt,mergeCommit: MERGED, c692b02) but the local side-effect (checkout main) failed on ORCH's own uncommitted handoffs/registry.json and orchestrator.log -- the same shape GIT_MERGE.md's worktree-variant section describes (read the actual gh pr view state before treating a local-side error as FAIL). Stashed those two files, completed local cleanup (checkout main, pull --ff-only, branch -D, remote ref delete), verified all five GIT_MERGE.md acceptance criteria, then restored the stash. One stash conflict: the untracked docs/issues/ISS-0212.yaml (a follow-on ORCH had filed but deferred committing) could not be restored because a DIFFERENT, properly-resolved version of that same path had already been merged to main by another concurrent session (ISS-0212 closed as a duplicate of the already-fixed ISS-0194) -- verified by diff that main's version is the real, independently-verified closure, and dropped the stale stashed copy rather than restoring over it.
artifacts_out: docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml is unaffected; no new artefact beyond the merge itself

issues.description: The dispatched ELIXIR-DEV agent stopped after claiming the handoff, stating it was 'waiting for a background test monitor' -- a subagent has no such async wake mechanism, so this dispatch pattern (spawn a long-running background test, then idle expecting a notification) will always stall a subagent this way. Worth a note in the relevant role file or dispatch guidance that subagents must poll/complete within their own tool-call loop, never assume a cross-turn notification.
